title: When Does On-Policy Interaction Help? Representational Tradeoffs in Value-Based Imitation Learning
abstract: arXiv:2607.29617v2 Announce Type: replace-cross  Abstract: Imitation learning (IL)---training an agent to replicate expert behavior from demonstrations---underpins applications from robotics to language model training. Standard approaches such as Behavior Cloning (BC) are known to suffer from compounding errors and performance plateaus, particularly when the learner cannot perfectly represent the expert's policy (as is typical, e.g., in distillation). Two interventions are widely understood empirically to improve performance: querying the expert interactively along the learner's own trajectories, and using value function estimation en route to generating a policy. translated_title: 同策略交互何时有益？基于价值的模仿学习中的表征权衡
translated_abstract: 模仿学习（IL）——即训练智能体从演示中复制专家行为——是机器人技术到语言模型训练等诸多应用的基础。众所周知，行为克隆（BC）等标准方法存在误差累积和性能停滞的问题，尤其当学习者无法完美表征专家策略时（例如在蒸馏场景中这是典型情况）。两种干预措施在经验上被广泛认为可以提升性能：沿学习者自身轨迹交互式地查询专家，以及在生成策略的过程中使用价值函数估计。我们研究了这些改进的本质及其可能令人惊讶的相互作用。我们的主要发现是，与专家的交互放宽了对学习者的表征要求：只需要一个能够实现专家价值函数的模型，从而绕过了（通常更严格的）实现专家策略的要求。（注：摘要原文在此处被截断）
tldr: 该论文发现，在基于价值的模仿学习中，与专家进行同策略交互能放宽对学习者的表征要求——只需模型能实现专家的价值函数，而无需实现要求更严格的专家策略本身。
en_tdlr: This paper shows that on-policy expert interaction relaxes the representational demands on the learner in value-based imitation learning—requiring only that the learner realize the expert's value function, bypassing the often stricter requirement of realizing the expert's policy itself.
